summary.headline: Inox Green Q4 FY26 total income INR120 crore (+40% YoY), EBITDA INR57 crore (+93%), with INR40 crore of acquisition-linked other income flattering profit.
summary.overview: Inox Green reported Q4 FY26 total income of INR120 crore, EBITDA of INR57 crore, PBT of INR46 crore and PAT of INR28 crore, with machine availability near 96.5%. Management said roughly INR40 crore of quarterly other income relates to the two pending O&M acquisitions (debt-linked income), with INR10 crore each from value-added services and treasury. Parent Inox Wind reported Q4 revenue of INR1,306 crore (flat YoY) and PAT of INR106 crore, and FY26 revenue of about INR4,500–4,600 crore against a revised INR5,000 crore target. Management guided FY27 consolidated revenue growth of about 75% and Inox Green EBITDA of above INR600 crore, while the evacuation-infrastructure demerger has been approved by NCLT Ahmedabad.

segments.name: Inox Green (O&M)
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 EBITDA INR57 crore on INR120 crore total income; portfolio above 13 GWp (about 10.5 GW wind, rest solar). Management said full-year turnover of INR426 crore gave EBITDA of about INR210 crore, roughly 50% margin, and Devansh Jain put the ex-acquisition-income margin at about 45%.

segments.name: Inox Wind (EPC/equipment)
segments.commentary: Q4 consolidated revenue INR1,306 crore (flat YoY) and EBITDA INR333 crore; order book 3.1 GW, with about 600 MW added in FY26. Order mix is about 50:50 turnkey to equipment supply, targeted to reach 75–80% equipment supply.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue growth of about 75% over FY26 (management also cited around 70–75%); Devansh Jain implied about INR7,500 crore revenue on the INR4,500 crore base.
Inox Green FY27 EBITDA guidance of upwards of INR600 crore, maintained after the investments fold into Inox Green's balance sheet.
EBITDA margin for Inox Wind guided at north of about 20%.

Inox Green expected to see a multifold rise in consolidated EBITDA and PAT in FY27 over FY26 once the two O&M acquisitions (about 6.5 GW) are consolidated; the first entity's order is expected within about two weeks, the second within 60–90 days.

Demerger of evacuation infrastructure business (gross block about INR1,000 crore, annual depreciation INR50–55 crore) into Inox Renewable Solutions expected to complete in about 1–2 months; dividend policy to follow consolidation.
New 4.4 MW turbine launch expected within calendar 2026, subject to approvals.
Inox Clean targets about 14 GW capacity by FY29, adding roughly 3 GW+ per year, of which 20–30% expected to be wind.
capex_capacity: Inox Green portfolio above 13 GWp, of which about 10.5 GW is wind; acquisition of about 6.5 GW of operational wind O&M assets from two companies is pending, with one entity's order expected in about two weeks.
Inox Wind's 3.1 GW order book supports more than 24 months of execution visibility; most EPC jobs expected to be complete by H1 FY27 except one leading job.
Backward integration: cranes about half in-house with a couple more coming this year; power transformer capacity ramped up; power electronics expansion planned.
Inox Clean: 10 GW IPP, 10 GW solar cell and 10 GW module targeted over next 15 months; about 2 GW installed IPP capacity; 6 GW module and 3 GW cell manufacturing capacity.
demand_pricing: Inox Wind order book 3.1 GW, of which about 500 MW is from Inox Clean (about 16%); Inox Clean orders expected to rise to about one-third of annual execution.
Management said equipment supply carries better working-capital terms (mostly LC-backed) and steel pass-through, and margins are more protected than in turnkey EPC.
Inox Green O&M margin about 50%; O&M expected to rise from about 10% to 18–20% of consolidated revenue after acquisitions.
PSU contracts saw payment delays; management said the PSU project issue is now resolved.
Working capital: management said net working capital days target of about 200 was missed; supply disruption for a key imported component (ECS) by ship and commodity price rises were cited.

qa_highlights.question: What EBITDA margin do the acquired O&M assets carry, and what is the FY27 Inox Green guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said both acquisitions have about 50% EBITDA margin as they are former OEMs with substations and evacuation systems; FY27 Inox Green EBITDA guidance is above INR600 crore.

qa_highlights.question: How is the INR600 crore FY27 EBITDA reached given acquisition timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Devansh Jain said entity one's order is due in about two weeks and entity two's within 60–90 days; revenues and profits from 1 April 2026 will be reflected in consolidated results. Management added about 1.5 GW of organic addition for Inox Wind plus value-added services.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q4 other income about INR61 crore, and how much is core?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about INR40 crore relates to the two acquisitions' debt, INR10 crore to value-added services and INR10 crore to treasury; PAT impact about INR25–26 crore. Devansh Jain said ex-acquisition income the margin would be about 45%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Inox Green revenue fall from INR78–82 crore in Q3 to INR69 crore in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the quarter-on-quarter move to value-added service lumpiness of about INR8–9 crore and asked investors to look at the annualised run rate.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Inox Wind moving from turnkey to equipment supply, and what happens to margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjeev Agarwal said turnkey caused the largest working capital blockage; order book moved from 100% turnkey to about 50:50, targeting 75–80% equipment supply. Management said margins stay above about 20% and equipment supply is more predictable.

qa_highlights.question: What was FY26 megawatt execution and status of working capital days?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give FY26 megawatt execution, reiterating revenue-based guidance; it reported INR4,600 crore against a INR5,000 crore target and said INR400 crore would be made up in Q1–Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Dividend policy and use of INR600 crore cash flow?
qa_highlights.answer: Devansh Jain said the Board will set a dividend policy after consolidation; the INR600 crore is expected to be operating cash flow with no depreciation or finance cost and a tax shield up to INR700 crore; acquisitions may use 10–20% of free cash flow.

risks_watch: Cash conversion: Inox Wind working capital and receivables (PSU delays) are behind the INR400 crore shortfall versus target; watch Q1 FY27 collections.
Quality of Inox Green earnings: about INR40 crore of Q4 other income is acquisition-linked; ex-that, margin is about 45% on annual basis.
Acquisition closure timing and NCLT/administrative approvals for the two O&M entities and the demerger.
Execution risk from geopolitical supply disruption (ECS imports by ship, commodity prices) and the one remaining major EPC job.
Governance and minority-shareholder concerns raised on value destruction, megawatt-to-revenue guidance changes and refusal to disclose FY26 MW execution.
summary.management_tone: Confident and expansive on strategy and FY27 growth, but defensive and evasive on FY26 execution (megawatts, working-capital shortfall), attributing misses to geopolitical and supply-chain factors.
key_quotes: We focus more on selected EPC project and less IPPs, a lot of customers are there who are doing their own IPPs, their own project, and we continue to limit our scope to equipment supply.
I think we were on the side of conservatism while doing this.

New 4.4 MW turbine launch, subject to approvals
Inox Clean 10 GW IPP, 10 GW solar cell and 10 GW module targeted over next 15 months (about 2 GW installed IPP today)

growth.why: Management guided ~75% FY27 consolidated revenue growth and Inox Green FY27 EBITDA above INR600 crore, backed by a 3.1 GW Inox Wind order book (>24 months visibility) and about 6.5 GW of pending O&M acquisitions, though the Q4 EBITDA/PAT surge is partly flattered by ~INR40 crore of acquisition-linked other income and the 75% target lacks a full capacity bridge.
